title: Cause and Result with fordi, derfor, and så
goal: Choose fordi, derfor, or så and keep the verb in the right position.

objectives.statement: Choose fordi, derfor, or så and keep the verb in the right position.

spans.value: Mina and Jonas work in the same office. They are preparing for an important meeting, but Mina arrives late and wet from the rain.
Bussen kom ikke fordi veien var stengt.

blocks.translation: The bus didn’t come because the road was closed.

spans.value: Å nei. Hvordan kom du deg hit?

blocks.translation: Oh no. How did you get here?

spans.value: Jeg ventet i tjue minutter, men det kom ingen buss. Derfor tok jeg taxi.

blocks.translation: I waited for twenty minutes, but no bus came. Therefore, I took a taxi.

spans.value: Møtet begynner snart, så vi må gå inn nå.

blocks.translation: The meeting starts soon, so we have to go in now.

spans.value: Jeg har ikke spist frokost fordi jeg hadde det travelt.

blocks.translation: I haven’t eaten breakfast because I was in a hurry.

spans.value: Det ligger noen rundstykker på kjøkkenet, så du kan ta med deg ett.

blocks.translation: There are some bread rolls in the kitchen, so you can take one with you.

spans.value: Takk! Jeg er veldig sulten. Derfor er det vanskelig å konsentrere seg.

blocks.translation: Thanks! I’m very hungry; therefore, it’s difficult to concentrate.

spans.value: The conversation contains three ways of connecting a cause with a result:

items.value: introduces the cause: why something happens.
points to the result as a consequence.
connects a situation directly to its result.

spans.value: The meaning is closely related, but the sentence structure is not the same.

no.value: Veien var stengt. Bussen kom ikke.

en.value: The road was closed. The bus didn’t come.

spans.value: You can connect them in three ways:

no.value: Bussen kom ikke fordi veien var stengt.

en.value: The bus didn’t come because the road was closed.

no.value: Veien var stengt. Derfor kom ikke bussen.

en.value: The road was closed. Therefore, the bus didn’t come.

no.value: Veien var stengt, så bussen kom ikke.

en.value: The road was closed, so the bus didn’t come.

spans.value: All three versions describe the same basic relationship. The choice depends on how you want to organize the information.
pattern practiced in this lesson, you state a result and then give its cause:
, you first state the cause. You then begin a new main clause by pointing to its consequence:
, you state the cause and connect it directly to a following main clause:
Choosing the right connector is only half the task. You must also place the verb correctly.
means because. It introduces a subordinate clause (leddsetning): a clause that functions as part of a larger sentence.

no.value: Mina tok taxi fordi bussen ikke kom.

en.value: Mina took a taxi because the bus did not come.

spans.value: The main information is that Mina took a taxi. The clause beginning with

no.value: Jeg blir hjemme fordi jeg er syk.

en.value: I’m staying home because I’m ill.

no.value: Vi lukket vinduet fordi det regnet.

en.value: We closed the window because it was raining.

no.value: Han kjøper mat på vei hjem fordi kjøleskapet er tomt.

en.value: He is buying food on the way home because the refrigerator is empty.

spans.value: In a simple positive clause, the word order after

no.value: fordi veien var stengt

en.value: because the road was closed

no.value: fordi jeg hadde det travelt

en.value: because I was in a hurry

spans.value: The important difference becomes especially visible with a sentence adverb such as
. In a subordinate clause introduced by
normally comes before the finite verb:

no.value: Jeg tok taxi fordi bussen ikke kom.

en.value: I took a taxi because the bus did not come.

no.value: Vi spiste hjemme fordi restauranten ikke var åpen.

en.value: We ate at home because the restaurant was not open.

no.value: Sara ringte legen fordi hun ikke følte seg bedre.

en.value: Sara called the doctor because she did not feel better.

spans.value: Compare a main clause and a fordi-clause:

no.value: Bussen kom ikke.

en.value: The bus did not come.

no.value: fordi bussen ikke kom

en.value: because the bus did not come

spans.value: A common mistake is to preserve main-clause order after

no.value: Jeg tok taxi fordi bussen kom ikke.

en.value: I took a taxi because the bus did not come.

spans.value: This is not standard word order here. The corrected version is:

no.value: Jeg tok taxi fordi bussen ikke kom.

en.value: I took a taxi because the bus did not come.

spans.value: Do not move every element mechanically. The key point is that
introduces a subordinate clause, and sentence adverbs such as

sections.title: Pointing to the result with derfor

spans.value: means therefore, for that reason, or that is why. It does not introduce a subordinate clause. It is usually placed at the beginning of a main clause and occupies the first position.
Norwegian main clauses follow the V2 rule: the finite verb comes in the second position. When
is first, the verb comes before the subject.

no.value: Veien var stengt. Derfor tok Mina taxi.

en.value: The road was closed. Therefore, Mina took a taxi.

no.value: Jeg sov dårlig. Derfor er jeg trøtt.

en.value: I slept badly. Therefore, I’m tired.

no.value: Hotellet var fullt. Derfor bestilte vi et annet rom.

en.value: The hotel was full. Therefore, we booked another room.

spans.value: Compare an ordinary subject-first main clause:

no.value: Mina tok taxi.

en.value: Mina took a taxi.

spans.value: takes the first position, the subject moves after the finite verb:

no.value: Derfor tok Mina taxi.

en.value: Therefore, Mina took a taxi.

spans.value: , main-clause order remains in place: finite verb before

no.value: Alarmen ringte ikke. Derfor våknet jeg ikke.

en.value: The alarm did not ring. Therefore, I did not wake up.

no.value: Butikken var stengt. Derfor kunne vi ikke kjøpe mat.

en.value: The shop was closed. Therefore, we could not buy food.

spans.value: A common mistake is to put both
and the subject before the finite verb:

no.value: Derfor Mina tok taxi.

en.value: Therefore, Mina took a taxi.

no.value: Derfor tok Mina taxi.

en.value: Therefore, Mina took a taxi.

spans.value: This is the same V2 pattern used when another element is placed first:

no.value: I dag tar Mina taxi.

en.value: Today Mina is taking a taxi.

no.value: Derfor tar Mina taxi.

en.value: Therefore Mina is taking a taxi.

sections.title: Connecting a cause and result with så

spans.value: means so. It joins a cause to a result without turning the result into a subordinate clause.

no.value: Møtet begynner snart, så vi må gå inn.

en.value: The meeting starts soon, so we have to go in.

no.value: Jeg var sulten, så jeg lagde middag.

en.value: I was hungry, so I made dinner.

no.value: Toget var forsinket, så vi kom for sent.

en.value: The train was delayed, so we arrived late.

spans.value: , the result is commonly expressed with ordinary subject-first main-clause order:

no.value: Det regnet, så vi tok bussen.

en.value: It was raining, so we took the bus.

no.value: Han fant ikke nøklene, så han kunne ikke låse døra.

en.value: He could not find the keys, so he could not lock the door.

no.value: Kaffen var kald, så jeg drakk den ikke.

en.value: The coffee was cold, so I did not drink it.

no.value: så han kunne ikke låse døra

en.value: so he could not lock the door

no.value: så jeg drakk den ikke

en.value: so I did not drink it

spans.value: These are main clauses. The finite verb comes before

no.value: Han ringte naboen fordi han ikke kunne låse døra.

en.value: He called the neighbor because he could not lock the door.

no.value: Han fant ikke nøklene, så han kunne ikke låse døra.

en.value: He could not find the keys, so he could not lock the door.

spans.value: A likely mistake is to treat

no.value: Det regnet, så tok vi bussen.

en.value: It was raining, so we took the bus.

spans.value: For the cause-and-result meaning taught here, use:

no.value: Det regnet, så vi tok bussen.

en.value: It was raining, so we took the bus.

spans.value: can have other functions in other contexts, but here it is the connector meaning so. Keep the cause before it and use a complete main clause after it.

sections.title: Three ways to describe the same relationship

spans.value: The three connectors can often describe the same situation, but they organize it differently.

no.value: Vi ble hjemme fordi det regnet.

en.value: We stayed home because it was raining.

spans.value: The listener first hears what happened: we stayed home. The
Starting with the cause and emphasizing its consequence

no.value: Det regnet. Derfor ble vi hjemme.

en.value: It was raining. Therefore, we stayed home.

spans.value: points back to it and presents the next statement as a consequence. Because

no.value: Det regnet, så vi ble hjemme.

en.value: It was raining, so we stayed home.

spans.value: The result follows naturally from the first statement. After result-linking

no.value: Nora dro tidlig fordi hun ikke følte seg bra.

en.value: Nora left early because she did not feel well.

no.value: Nora følte seg ikke bra. Derfor dro hun tidlig.

en.value: Nora did not feel well. Therefore, she left early.

no.value: Nora følte seg ikke bra, så hun dro tidlig.

en.value: Nora did not feel well, so she left early.

spans.value: The connector changes the direction in which the information is presented:

items.value: In the postposed pattern practiced here,
presents the result before its cause.
looks back at a cause and introduces its result.
moves directly from a cause to its result.

sections.title: Connector and word order must work together

spans.value: It is not enough to choose a connector by translating an English word. Each connector creates or signals a particular structure.

no.value: Jeg gikk hjem fordi jeg ikke følte meg bra.

en.value: I went home because I did not feel well.

no.value: Jeg følte meg ikke bra. Derfor gikk jeg hjem.

en.value: I did not feel well. Therefore, I went home.

no.value: Jeg følte meg ikke bra, så jeg gikk hjem.

en.value: I did not feel well, so I went home.

no.value: Vi avlyste turen fordi været var dårlig.

en.value: We canceled the trip because the weather was bad.

no.value: Været var dårlig. Derfor avlyste vi turen.

en.value: The weather was bad. Therefore, we canceled the trip.

no.value: Været var dårlig, så vi avlyste turen.

en.value: The weather was bad, so we canceled the trip.

spans.value: , the difference between main-clause and subordinate-clause order may be less obvious. The
sentence still clearly shows V2 inversion:
Mina has eaten a bread roll, and the meeting has ended.
Ja, men jeg var nervøs fordi jeg ikke hadde lest den siste rapporten.

blocks.translation: Yes, but I was nervous because I had not read the latest report.

spans.value: Du forklarte prosjektet tydelig, så alle forsto planen.

blocks.translation: You explained the project clearly, so everyone understood the plan.

spans.value: Kunden stilte mange spørsmål. Derfor varte møtet lenger enn planlagt.

blocks.translation: The client asked many questions. Therefore, the meeting lasted longer than planned.

spans.value: Nå er jeg sulten fordi jeg ikke tok noe rundstykke.

blocks.translation: Now I’m hungry because I didn’t take a bread roll.

spans.value: Kafeen ved siden av er fortsatt åpen, så vi kan spise lunsj der.

blocks.translation: The café next door is still open, so we can eat lunch there.

spans.value: The same forms now help Mina and Jonas explain feelings, evaluate the meeting, and make a new plan.
introduces the reason for her nervousness:

no.value: fordi jeg ikke hadde lest den siste rapporten

en.value: because I had not read the latest report

spans.value: connects Mina’s clear explanation to its result:

no.value: så alle forsto planen

en.value: so everyone understood the plan

spans.value: begins a result sentence and triggers inversion:

no.value: Derfor varte møtet lenger.

en.value: Therefore, the meeting lasted longer.

spans.value: Emil is hosting dinner for two friends. The supermarket closes earlier than he expected. He cannot buy one ingredient, changes the recipe, and serves dinner later than planned.
This new situation supports all three information patterns:

no.value: Emil endret oppskriften fordi butikken ikke var åpen.

en.value: Emil changed the recipe because the shop was not open.

no.value: Butikken var ikke åpen. Derfor endret Emil oppskriften.

en.value: The shop was not open. Therefore, Emil changed the recipe.

no.value: Butikken var ikke åpen, så Emil endret oppskriften.

en.value: The shop was not open, so Emil changed the recipe.

spans.value: A later event may create another result:

no.value: Middagen var ikke ferdig, så gjestene måtte vente.

en.value: Dinner was not ready, so the guests had to wait.

spans.value: The same fact can instead be presented as the reason:

no.value: Gjestene måtte vente fordi middagen ikke var ferdig.

en.value: The guests had to wait because dinner was not ready.

spans.value: Or the consequence can be highlighted in a separate sentence:

no.value: Middagen var ikke ferdig. Derfor måtte gjestene vente.

en.value: Dinner was not ready. Therefore, the guests had to wait.

prompt.value: Read three everyday cause-and-result situations. Choose the set that puts each result first, places the information answering why after fordi, and begins each reason clause at fordi. The scored evidence is cause-and-result meaning and connector choice; word order is context only.

options.text: Mina tok taxi. Derfor kom ikke bussen. Det regnet. Derfor ble vi hjemme. Nora følte seg ikke bra. Derfor dro hun tidlig.
options.why: This set uses derfor instead of a postposed fordi clause and reverses the first cause-and-result relation.

options.text: Mina tok taxi fordi bussen ikke kom. Vi ble hjemme fordi det regnet. Nora dro tidlig fordi hun ikke følte seg bra.
options.why: Each line puts the result first, then uses fordi to begin the reason that answers why.

options.text: Mina tok taxi, så bussen ikke kom. Det regnet, så vi ble hjemme. Nora følte seg ikke bra, så hun dro tidlig.
options.why: This set uses så with cause-first order instead of the requested result-first fordi pattern.

stem.value: Which set correctly expresses these three relationships in Norwegian? 1. Mina took a taxi because the bus did not come. 2. We stayed home because it was raining. 3. Nora left early because she did not feel well.

prompt.value: Complete each Norwegian sentence. The meanings are: I took a taxi because the bus did not come; We ate at home because the restaurant was not open. Choose the subordinate clause after fordi. The scored form is fordi + subject + ikke + finite verb.

explanation.value: After «fordi», use subordinate order with «ikke» before the finite verb. Sentence-initial «derfor» triggers verb–subject inversion, while result-linking «så» is followed by ordinary subject–verb order.

prompt.value: Complete each result sentence. The meanings are: The road was closed; therefore Mina took a taxi. The hotel was full; therefore we booked another room. After initial derfor, place the finite verb before the subject.

Complete each cause-and-result sentence. The meanings are: It was raining, so we took the bus. He could not find the keys, so he could not lock the door. After result-linking så, keep the subject before the finite verb and keep the finite verb before ikke in the result clause.

Choose the set that matches each information order: result plus reason with fordi; cause plus a separate result beginning with Derfor; cause plus a directly linked result with så. Score connector meaning and information order; the verb positions are shown but are not the primary evidence.

options.text: Vi avlyste turen fordi været var dårlig. Været var dårlig. Derfor avlyste vi turen. Været var dårlig, så vi avlyste turen.
options.why: The three lines use fordi for a following reason, derfor for a separate consequence, and så for a directly linked result.

options.text: Vi avlyste turen fordi været var dårlig. Været var dårlig, så vi avlyste turen. Været var dårlig. Derfor avlyste vi turen.
options.why: The second and third lines assign så and derfor to the wrong information orders.

options.text: Været var dårlig fordi vi avlyste turen. Været var dårlig. Derfor avlyste vi turen. Været var dårlig, så vi avlyste turen.
options.why: The first line reverses the intended result-and-reason relationship instead of placing the result before its fordi-clause.

stem.value: Which set correctly expresses these three relationships in Norwegian? 1. We canceled the trip because the weather was bad. 2. The weather was bad. Therefore, we canceled the trip. 3. The weather was bad, so we canceled the trip.

prompt.value: Build the Norwegian sentence meaning I went home because I did not feel well. Use every token exactly once. Show the postposed reason with fordi and subordinate order with ikke before the finite verb.

Reconstruct four Norwegian utterances from Mina and Jonas's follow-up exchange in this order: Mina gives a reason for being nervous; Jonas links a clear explanation to its result; Mina states that the client asked questions; Mina highlights the consequence with a sentence-initial result marker. Use every token exactly once. Preserve the appropriate connector and verb position in each utterance. Punctuation is attached to tokens.

Build three connected Norwegian sentences about Emil's changed dinner plan. Express that he changed the recipe because the supermarket was not open, therefore he served dinner later, and dinner was not ready so the guests had to wait. Use every token exactly once. Preserve postposed fordi with subordinate-clause order, sentence-initial Derfor with inversion, and så with a subject-first result clause. Punctuation is attached to tokens.

Build one Norwegian retrieval response expressing the same transport relationship in three forms: first Jonas arrived late because the train was delayed; next state the cause and consequence with a separate sentence followed by sentence-initial Derfor; finally connect the cause and result with så. Use every token exactly once and preserve each word-order pattern. Punctuation is attached to tokens.
